arxiv-1712-00015.title: Cavity quantum electrodynamics in the non-perturbative regime
arxiv-1712-00015.creator: Daniele De Bernardis, Tuomas Jaako, and Peter Rabl
arxiv-1712-00015.description: Abstract We study a generic cavity-QED system where a set of (artificial) two-level dipoles is coupled to the electric field of a single-mode L ​ C LC resonator. This setup is used to derive a minimal quantum mechanical model for cavity QED, which accounts for both dipole-field and direct dipole-dipole interactions.

arxiv-2006-16967.title: Lest We Forget: A Dataset of Coronavirus-Related News Headlines in Swiss Media
arxiv-2006-16967.creator: Alireza Ghasemi, Amina Chebira
arxiv-2006-16967.description: Abstract We release our COVID-19 news dataset, containing more than 10,000 links to news articles related to the Coronavirus pandemic published in the Swiss media since early January 2020. This collection can prove beneficial in mining and analysis of the reaction of the Swiss media to the COVID-19 pandemic and extracting insightful information for further research.

arxiv-2111-00910.title: Flag Codes: Distance Vectors and Cardinality Bounds
arxiv-2111-00910.creator: Clementa Alonso-González, Miguel Ángel Navarro-Pérez
arxiv-2111-00910.description: Abstract Given 𝔽 q {\mathbb{F}}_{q} the finite field with q q elements and an integer n ⩾ 2 n\geqslant 2 , a flag is a sequence of nested subspaces of 𝔽 q n {\mathbb{F}}_{q}^{n} and a flag code is a nonempty set of flags. In this context, the distance between flags is the sum of the corresponding subspace distances.

arxiv-2312-12277.title: Travelling pulses on three spatial scales in a Klausmeier-type vegetation-autotoxicity model
arxiv-2312-12277.creator: Paul Carter, Arjen Doelman, Annalisa Iuorio, Frits Veerman
arxiv-2312-12277.description: Abstract Reaction-diffusion models describing interactions between vegetation and water reveal the emergence of several types of patterns and travelling wave solutions corresponding to structures observed in real-life. Increasing their accuracy by also considering the ecological factor known as autotoxicity has lead to more involved models supporting the existence of complex dynamic patterns.

arxiv-2403-11277.title: Bifurcation Analysis of an Influenza A (H1N1) Model with Treatment and Vaccination
arxiv-2403-11277.creator: Kazi Mehedi Mohammad, Asma Akter Akhi, Md. Kamrujjaman
arxiv-2403-11277.description: Abstract Abstract. This study focuses on the modeling, mathematical analysis, developing theories, and numerical simulation of Influenza virus transmission. We have proved the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness of the solutions. Also, investigate the qualitative behavior of the models and find the basic reproduction number (\mathcal{R}_{0}) that guarantees the asymptotic stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibrium points.

arxiv-2406-07217.title: A Synthetic Dataset for Personal Attribute Inference
arxiv-2406-07217.creator: Hanna Yukhymenko, Robin Staab, Mark Vero, Martin Vechev
arxiv-2406-07217.description: Abstract Recently, powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) have become easily accessible to hundreds of millions of users world-wide. However, their strong capabilities and vast world knowledge do not come without associated privacy risks. In this work, we focus on the emerging privacy threat LLMs pose—the ability to accurately infer personal information from online texts.

arxiv-2410-14623.description: Abstract Context. Current and future large scale structure surveys aim to constrain the neutrino mass and the equation of state of dark energy. arxiv-2503-19513.creator: Franz Waltenberger, Angelina Voggenreiter, Martin Paul Wessel, Juergen Pfeffer

pmc-10633908.title: ILIAD: a suite of automated Snakemake workflows for processing genomic data for downstream applications
pmc-10633908.creator: Noah Herrick, Susan Walsh
pmc-10633908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundProcessing raw genomic data for downstream applications such as imputation, association studies, and modeling requires numerous third-party bioinformatics software tools. It is highly time-consuming and resource-intensive with computational demands and storage limitations that pose significant challenges that increase cost. The use of software tools independent of one another, in a disjointed stepwise fashion, increases the difficulty and sets forth higher error rates because of fragmented job executions in alignment, variant calling, and/or build conversion complications.

pmc-11673888.title: Association of Small HDL Subclasses with Mortality Risk in Chronic Kidney Disease
pmc-11673888.creator: Julia T Stadler, Andrea Borenich, Anja Pammer, Insa E Emrich, Hansjörg Habisch, Tobias Madl, Gunnar H Heine, Gunther Marsche, Carlo Cervellati, Judit Marsillach
pmc-11673888.description: High-density lipoproteins (HDL) exist in various subclasses, with smaller HDL particles possessing the highest anti-oxidative and anti-inflammatory properties. Understanding the role of these specific subclasses in chronic kidney disease (CKD) could provide valuable insights into disease progression and potential therapeutic targets.

pmc-12566163.title: Cervical Hyperextension Causes Acute Cerebral Congestion in Non-Anesthetized Healthy Adults: An Observational Self-Controlled Design Study
pmc-12566163.creator: Ozlem Ersoy Karka, Derya Guclu, Ilknur S Yorulmaz, Mehmet A Sungur, Gizem Demir Senoglu, Gulbin Sezen, Yavuz Demiraran, Enrico Mario Camporesi
pmc-12566163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: Severe complications associated with cervical hyperextension during general anesthesia have been reported. The question is whether some of the cerebral/spinal ischemic complications could be partially related to the position itself. Cerebral oximetric monitoring, combined with optic nerve sheath diameter and cognitive function in non-anesthetized healthy volunteers, should provide more extensive information about the effects of cervical hyperextension, independent of anesthesia. Materials and Methods: 51 healthy volunteers with no vertebrobasilar abnormalities completed the study and were included in statistical analysis.

pmc-12651397.title: Rational design of caffeic acid amides as novel antioxidants in lipid systems: Experimental and theoretical studies
pmc-12651397.creator: Zhiheng Yuan, Qicheng Sun, Yaoyao Zhang, Sichang Ti, Meimei Shan, Yang Xiao, Shangde Sun
pmc-12651397.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Caffeic acid (CA), known as a natural phenolic compound, is widely recognized for its antioxidant properties and potential applications in food preservation. However, its practical antioxidant efficacy and potential applications have been limited due to its poor lipophilicity. To overcome this issue, based on the hydrophobic residue structure and antioxidant activity of amino acids, three amino acids (methionine, tyrosine, and tryptophan) were screened for amidation with CA to both improve the lipophilicity of CA and enhance its antioxidant performance.

pmc-12755884.title: Hybridization breaks species barriers in long-term coevolution of a cyanobacterial population
pmc-12755884.creator: Gabriel Birzu, Harihara Subrahmaniam Muralidharan, Danielle Goudeau, Rex R Malmstrom, Daniel S Fisher, Devaki Bhaya, Detlef Weigel, Gabriel Birzu, Harihara Subrahmaniam Muralidharan, Danielle Goudeau, Rex R Malmstrom, Daniel S Fisher, Devaki Bhaya
pmc-12755884.description: Bacterial species often undergo rampant recombination yet maintain cohesive genomic identity. Ecological differences can generate recombination barriers between species and sustain genomic clusters in the short term. But can these forces prevent genomic mixing during long-term coevolution? Cyanobacteria in Yellowstone hot springs comprise several diverse species that have coevolved for hundreds of thousands of years, providing a rare natural experiment.

pmc-13388784.creator: Ao Xia, Jingyuan Liu, Juanjuan Song, Yu Han, Bingjie Ding, Ao Xie, Chang Liu, Xiance Tang, Wenqun Xing, Dongmin Zhou, Liu Liu, Hu Zhou
pmc-13388784.description: BackgroundVenous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common complication in patients with lung cancer and remains difficult to predict accurately using existing risk assessment tools. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for individualized prediction of VTE risk in patients with lung cancer.

pmc-13467427.title: Hepatic SIRT6 Deficiency Accelerates Female-Specific Aging Through SULT1E1-Mediated Estrogen Depletion
pmc-13467427.creator: Yonghui Liu, Ziliang Zhang, Tingting Wang, Xiuyan Yang, Qiufen Zhang, Xinyi Liu, Xuefeng Lu, Jian Zhang, Li Feng
pmc-13467427.description: Sexual dimorphism is a fundamental feature of aging, yet the liver-centric mechanisms underlying sex-specific aging trajectories remain incompletely understood. SIRT6, a NAD+-dependent deacetylase, is a master regulator of genome stability, metabolic homeostasis, and longevity. However, its cell-type- and sex-specific functions in aging have not been fully characterized.
